text: Fit the two lower-frequency spectral branches' amplitude-vs-temperature decay to the expected thermal-damping form.
Lighter branch effective mass = 0.039 +- 0.002 electron masses.
Lighter branch per-window fits scattered between 0.032 and 0.049 electron masses.
Heavier branch effective mass = 0.048 +- 0.003 electron masses.
Heavier branch per-window fits were stable at 0.048-0.049 electron masses across field windows.
Aborted the first gatemap attempt after its opening rows because the lock-in railed (~2.2 kOhm) against a 2 kOhm full-scale along the charge-neutrality ridge at large displacement field.
Re-ran the identical map at a five-times-larger full-scale (100 microV instead of 20 microV).
This re-run choice explicitly traded away low-resistance readout resolution to avoid saturating the higher-resistance ridge region.
A second, nearly vertical resistance ridge appears in the full gate map that depends only on the top gate, independent of back-gate voltage.
This second ridge is interpreted as a top-gate-only-gated segment of the current path lying outside the back gate's footprint.
This second ridge is distinct from the true dual-gated channel neutrality point.
Concluded the earlier single-gate liveness-leg peaks had actually been reading this segment's own neutrality point, not the channel's.
Chose to pursue the electron-doped side of the zero-displacement-field line for subsequent field-dependence work.
Reasoned the hole side is confined to a low-density exception regime because of the top-gate voltage limit.
Reasoned the hole side is also confined by the top-gate-only series segment approaching its own neutrality there.
Spacing of integer quantum-Hall ladder minima above 4.5 T in the hole-side spot check gives an independently derived density scale of roughly 0.80-0.92 relative to the geometry-prior calibration.
This 0.80-0.92 range brackets the 0.886 scale independently obtained from the electron-side Luttinger-sum analysis.
Fitting the dominant ridge's slope in the gatemap's operating window gives a data-calibrated back-gate/top-gate capacitance ratio of 0.773.
This is about 11% below the geometry-prior value (~0.864).
The discrepancy was judged most likely to reflect an hBN-thickness error in the prior rather than a wiring/contact-role transposition.
The fourfold-degeneracy density scale (0.886) from electron-side fan/spot-check data is consistent with the independent scale (0.80-0.92) from the hole-side integer-quantum-Hall ladder spacing.
Taken together, this consistency is read as evidence of no spin/valley (flavor) polarization at this gate/field operating point.
Formally located the oscillation onset at 2.4 T, carried by the stronger of two candidate tones.
A second, weaker candidate onset track was called marginal.
FFT spectrum shows peaks at 6.2, 21.8, 28.1, and 15.6 T.
A weaker peak at 37.4 T is also present.
The three strongest peaks were checked as stable across two different background-subtraction/window choices.
The mass fitted for the combined (sum-frequency) tone (0.051-0.069) is heavier than the heavy branch.
In the upper field window, the sum-tone mass approaches the sum of the light and heavy branch masses.
Because the sum-tone mass is heavier than the light branch alone, a simple 'beat' interpretation (two closely spaced frequencies from a single pocket) was excluded.
This exclusion is read as a decisive indicator of two genuinely distinct Fermi pockets plus a combination orbit, rather than a separate third pocket.
Planned a cheapest-first discriminator sequence given the density-map result left the two-scenario question unresolved.
First step: a short, low-field spot check targeting the predicted frequency band of the light pocket at fine field resolution.
This was chosen to precede committing several hours to a temperature-dependence (effective-mass) measurement.
Reasoning: a sufficiently light pocket should still be visible at the achieved electron temperature down at sub-tesla fields, so a clean null result there would be informative.
Designed the first zero-field gatemap: full top-gate range at 20 mV steps (66 points).
Back-gate range from its negative limit up to +1.2 V (not the full +2.0 V limit) at 40 mV steps (63 rows).
Back-gate coverage was deliberately truncated because the geometry prior predicted that region would be metallic and uninformative for the charge-neutrality line or fan.
This truncation saved roughly 35 minutes.
Sensitivity set to 20 microV, fast delay 1 s, slow delay 3 s, leak guard active.
Committed a corrected displacement-field zero-point offset for all subsequent 'true zero displacement field' sweeps.
Offset derived from where the charge-neutrality-point ridge resistance reaches a symmetric minimum versus displacement field.
This corrected offset replaces the nominal (as-designed) zero point.
All three resistance channels agree on the same two oscillation-frequency peaks (~7-8 T and ~17-18 T), stable against changes to background-subtraction settings.

This resolves the earlier concern that the weakest channel showed different content; the earlier divergence is now attributed to insufficient signal in a partial record, not a real cross-channel discrepancy.
A weak line near the sum of the two frequencies is also noted.
A sub-threshold lower frequency is also noted.
Reading 1: the two main frequencies as a bound pair of pockets, at a relative-amplitude split the agent calls strained against a specific model's prediction.
Reading 2: the higher frequency alone as a single Fermi surface, with the lower frequency left unexplained.

Reading 3: the higher frequency as a second harmonic of the lower, disfavored because expected thermal damping at the achieved electron temperature should suppress a harmonic well below its fundamental, yet the two measured amplitudes are comparable.
Designed and launched the first field-dependent oscillation spot check at a single fixed density near one edge of the zero-displacement-field window.
Swept magnetic field from just below a heuristic onset estimate up toward the field cap.
Used uniform field steps sized from the calibrated density's expected oscillation frequency.
The heavier SdH tone's fitted mass depends on which part of the field window is used: ~0.038 (lower half), ~0.057 (upper half), 0.041 (full window).
This field-window dependence is reported as an unresolved fork rather than a single value.
The resulting light-to-heavy mass ratio (1.4-2.0) falls short of the ABAB model's predicted ratio of about 2.2 at this density.
Fitting the neutrality-point line across the 2D map gives a gate-capacitance ratio ~3.7% larger than the value predicted from the stacked-dielectric geometry.
This 3.7% difference is called a pass of a geometry sanity check.
The two more sensitive channels agree on this ratio to about 0.4%.
The absolute density scale is left anchored to the geometry-derived single-gate capacitance, pending an independent (quantum-Hall) cross-check.
This combination (ratio + anchored scale) is used to compute a zero-displacement-field density window and the expected oscillation-frequency scale at its edges.

A faint, gate-voltage-only feature (not displacement-field-dependent) appears in the 2D map at a fixed value of the fast-axis gate, present across every slow-axis value, located away from the density corridor of interest.
Interpreted as a spatially localized region of the device gated by only one of the two gates (e.g., an arm not covered by one gate layer), rather than a bulk electronic feature.
Flagged as a device-inhomogeneity note without further investigation this session.
Judged the six-rung temperature ladder to have adequately covered its intended range.
Each rung's realized sample temperature met the stability-acceptance criterion and stayed within 0.05 K of that value during its field sweep.
By the top rung, all three tracked spectral amplitudes had fallen onto the declining side of the expected thermal-damping curve.
The lowest-mass branch's amplitude only just reached the design threshold judged necessary for a reliable mass fit at the top rung, flagged as the weakest link in the coverage.
Designed a coarse 2D gate map across the full accessible gate box (back gate slow axis, top gate fast axis at finer resolution) to trace the displacement-field dependence of the resistance peak.
Reasoning: an exponential rise with |D| would indicate one candidate stacking order.
Reasoning: a modest field-symmetric rise would indicate a second candidate stacking order.
Reasoning: a field-asymmetric rise would indicate a third candidate stacking order.
This map was designed as the session's first stacking-order discriminator.
Chose to use the necessary field descent from the cap to measure a second field-dependent sweep, rather than ramping back to zero field and re-ramping at a different gate setting.
The descent sweep was taken along a gate line at a finite displacement field corresponding to the knee of the field-independent resistance plateau identified earlier.
Reasoning: this would test the Landau-level structure of the gapped state.
Reasoning: this would also test whether the zero-field plateau was carrying its own parallel conduction path.
On the opposite-carrier-sign spot check, oscillation onset occurs at a somewhat higher field than the first side.
A dominant low frequency and a weaker higher frequency (~38% of the dominant peak's amplitude) are found.

The higher frequency scales with density between the two sides consistent with a real Fermi surface tracking the expected area-density relation (density ratio matches frequency ratio to within a few percent).
The lower frequency survives and dominates on this side, where the bound-pair model predicts it should nearly vanish.
Confirmed the lower frequency is not a harmonic of the higher frequency (no longer an exact half/double relationship once measured independently on this side).
Both findings actively strain, rather than resolve, the three-way structural fork carried from the first spot check.
From the device-card gate-stack geometry alone (pre-measurement), the D=0 line's density window was predicted to reach ~+3.5e12 cm^-2 on the electron side.
And only ~-1.0e12 cm^-2 magnitude on the hole side, given the gate-voltage limits.
Therefore the investigation was expected to end up electron-side-biased, unless the charge-neutrality point sat well off zero gate voltage.
Fitting oscillation-amplitude decay across temperature rungs on the resolved branch gives an effective mass ~18% below one candidate model value, with small statistical uncertainty.
This is called consistent with that model value, within the model's own parameter uncertainty.
The fit strongly excludes a second, much heavier candidate model value, since it would predict a residual amplitude at the highest rung roughly 50x smaller than what is actually measured.
The half-frequency modulation component's independently fit effective mass is statistically identical to the main branch's.
This supports identifying the half-frequency component as an amplitude-modulation feature of the same Landau-level ladder, rather than a separate carrier pocket.
Second- and third-harmonic frequency combs of the main branch are identified in the spectra and screened out rather than mistaken for independent oscillation content.

Across the whole density range on both sensitive channels, the map shows only one real, density-linear (through-origin) oscillation branch, running at ~87-90% of the frequency scale implied by the calibrated density.
A second, lower frequency seen in the single-density checks sits locked at exactly half that branch's frequency at every density where it can be measured, rather than tracing its own curve.
This locked half-frequency feature is interpreted as a modulation feature of the same Landau-level ladder, rather than an independent pocket.
The one branch alone accounts for the full expected carrier density at a single overall scale factor.
Two competing structural readings remain indistinguishable at this resolution: a specific fractional pocket at that same scale, versus a single full surface at a very similar rescaled amplitude.
This indistinguishability is because the specific lighter, small pocket that would discriminate between them could show at most about one oscillation period in this map's field window.
The agent explicitly frames this as 'searched but not resolvable,' not as evidence of absence.
The fainter, more lightly doped secondary region (probed only in series with the dominant region through the same voltage-probe pair) was judged uninformative on its own for the stacking call.
Reason: no tone set attributable solely to it was resolved.
Its predicted tones (shifted to somewhat higher frequency than the dominant region's) were judged to fall within the frequency resolution of the dominant region's tones, at low relative weight.
Direct comparison of the two spot checks at the same field value shows the second side is substantially more resistive than the first (~14-15 kOhm vs ~5 kOhm).
This is read as indicating a genuine carrier-sign asymmetry in this device's transport, beyond the sign difference expected from the oscillation pattern alone.
Final call for the one measured contact pair: Bernal (ABAB) stacking, stated as a strong determination.
Based on a saturating, meV-scale, field-symmetric neutrality-point gap.
Based on a four-fold degenerate Landau-level sequence with zero-state crossings at zero displacement field.
Based on a displacement-field-split two-fold sequence with a monotonic zero-state at finite displacement field.
Based on the temperature-activation results.
All evaluated on the session's own in-session density and displacement-field calibration.
No other region of the device was measurable this session, since every other spare contact pair was dead or unconnected as provided.
The call is explicitly scoped to the single measured region.
Designed and launched an ascending temperature-dependence measurement (oscillation-amplitude-vs-temperature ladder) on the single resolved density-linear branch at a fixed density.
Chose rung temperatures spanning the range needed to separate two specific candidate effective-mass values by their predicted amplitude damping.
Included a stability-based equilibration check before each rung's field sweep.
Included a rule to extend to a higher temperature live if the highest planned rung still showed unexpectedly large oscillation amplitude.
The dedicated high-quality descent sweep at the extreme density directly confirms the light branch at a specific frequency.
This is used to exclude an alternative explanation in which the low- and high-frequency peaks are actually a magnetic-breakdown sum/difference pair rather than two independent branches.

Reasoning: a breakdown orbit's amplitude should damp with the combined effective mass of its parent orbits, but the shared high-frequency tone here is measured to be lighter, not heavier, than such a parent would require.
A nearby weaker peak sits at exactly the arithmetic difference (not sum) of the two main frequencies, consistent with a mixing artifact rather than a genuine third branch.
The half-frequency modulation component's mass still matches its parent branch, distinguishing it from what a genuine second harmonic of the new light branch would show.
Designed and ran an SdH spot check on the electron side at fixed density +3.2e12 cm^-2 (D=0).
Field swept from 0 to 10 T: 50 mT steps to 1 T, then 10 mT steps above (921 points total).
Lock-in sensitivity fixed at 50 microV; delay set to zero, relying only on the magnet driver's built-in settle.
Priced at about 2 h 15 m.
Deliberately left the gates parked at the spot and field at 10 T at the end so the hole-side check could ride the magnet back down without re-traversing the range.
The top-gate-only series-segment resistance maximum is unchanged between the two auxiliary-gate settings at three sampled top-gate voltages.
The true dual-gated neutrality point responded strongly to the auxiliary gate.
The high-density flank also responded strongly to the auxiliary gate.
Concluded the series segment is not part of the auxiliary-gate-coupled contact regions and so cannot be gated away by it.
A single scale factor fit to ~257 resistance-minima positions gave a carrier-density calibration about 18% below the geometry-based estimate.
This is consistent with the gate-capacitance-ratio discrepancy found earlier.
On that scale the minima cluster in steps of four, with the +/-4 levels tracked down to the lowest resolvable fields.
This is read as the single-particle degenerate Landau-level sequence of one candidate stacking order.
Rather than the alternative candidate's expected pattern, which would instead show its lowest robust levels only at higher filling factor.
Based on the ABAB stacking call, recommended deprioritizing further correlated/flat-band-physics investigation of this device.
Recommended redirecting future campaign value toward conventional quantum-Hall degeneracy-lifting physics instead.
Noted the device already showed full quantum-Hall symmetry breaking by 5 T at low density on the hole side.
Across the full temperature ladder, the neutrality-point resistance stayed flat with temperature below ~7 K at every displacement-field point.
Resistance then fell gently at the two most-gapped points.
Arrhenius activation energies of roughly 1.8 meV and 1.2 meV at those two points.
Essentially no activation (flat or slightly rising resistance) at the reference point and the two more weakly gapped points.
Gap scale was read as meV-sized and only weakly dependent on displacement field.
Large non-vanishing resistance extrapolated to infinite temperature, consistent with thermally assisted conduction over a small, saturating gap.
This specifically excludes the tens-of-meV activation energy and order-of-magnitude resistance collapse expected for one candidate stacking order (a roughly threefold change was observed instead).
Campaign call upgraded from 'strong' to 'strong, two-branch' for the same channel and stacking-order assignment.
Both the originally-called branch and the newly resolved light branch are now treated as directly observed evidence for the same order.
This retires the earlier hedge that the light pocket was unresolved.
The competing single-rescaled-surface reading is now stated to be fully dissolved under the revised scale.
Attributed to the light branch having been unresolved at the time, rather than to a genuine single-surface degeneracy.
Remaining softness: the light branch's own effective mass is still unmeasured.
Remaining softness: the absolute density-scale calibration is still pending an independent cross-check.
Judged the device alive on the wired current path from the four single-gate liveness legs.
Drain current stayed at 9.8-9.97 nA (full bias reaching the drain) on every leg.
Pickup channel read 60-320 ohms, smooth and structured, on all four legs.
The contact pair was judged alive and ohmic over a full top-gate sweep at zero back-gate voltage.
Longitudinal resistance ran only about 40-370 ohm with no charge-neutrality peak in that cut.
The monotonic resistance trend was read as the device being electron-doped at zero back-gate voltage.
The neutrality point was inferred to lie outside the swept top-gate window.
Committed to an approximately eight-hour, six-rung temperature ladder at the fixed electron-side gate point (ascending nominal setpoints, alternating field-sweep direction each rung).
Included automatic stability and thermal-runaway guards, with heaters forced off on any early exit.
Chose to proceed without a confirmed remaining-cryogen figure from the operator, after asking for it and not receiving an answer.
Relied on the standing autonomy grant and the operator's ability to halt any individual rung.
Ramping the silicon gate from zero toward one polarity of its card limit does not open the source-drain contact.
Drain current stays pinned near its zero-gate baseline (~88 pA) across the entire sweep.
Sum-frequency tone's fitted mass is strongly field-window-dependent: 0.051 +- 0.003 electron masses (low-field window) vs 0.100 +- 0.010 electron masses (mid-field window).
Jointly reported as 0.065 +- 0.004 electron masses.
Attributed the discrepancy to the low-field window's peak being contaminated by the nearby heavier fundamental.
Treated the mid-field value as the clean read because it approximately equals the sum of the two fundamental branch masses.
Designed and launched a 2D density-versus-field oscillation map on the first (cleaner-signal, lower-onset) carrier-sign side.

Explicitly intended to distinguish a real second Fermi pocket (which should trace its own density-dependent frequency curve) from a harmonic (which would track an exact multiple of another branch) or an algebraic sum/mixing artifact.

The top of the originally planned density range had to be trimmed after applying the newly committed displacement-field correction, because the original edge would have driven the swept gate outside its validated range.
This was caught by a design-time check before any hardware moved.
The fine map refit the neutrality-ridge slope, giving an updated gate-capacitance ratio that supersedes the coarse-map estimate.
Located the true resistance minimum, adopted as the session's displacement-field-zero reference point.
Referenced to that point, the negative-to-positive field resistance ratio was about 0.85-0.90 over the reachable overlapping range.
This ratio was read as no sign of a strong field-sign asymmetry.
The positive side climbed about fourteenfold to roughly 3.4 kOhm before saturating flat to the edge of the sweep.
The peak narrowed from a broad ~150-220 mV window near the reference point to a sharp ~45 mV once gapped.
Ran two short top-gate linecuts at fixed back-gate voltage and 10 T field: one with the auxiliary gate at 0 V, one at its positive limit.
Specifically to test whether the top-gate-only series segment identified in the gate map is coupled to the auxiliary gate.
Done before committing further field-sweep time to a full density fan.
Designed and ran a second SdH spot check on the hole side, at the most negative density reachable on the D=0 line within the gate limits (about -1.2e12 cm^-2).
Rode the magnet down from 10 T to 0.3 T at 20 mT steps (486 points), sensitivity 50 microV.
Explicitly framed as a cheap, non-decisive preview rather than a decisive test.
Reason: a null result there would be resolution- and mass-limited rather than genuine evidence against the alternative stacking.
Attempted an independent cross-check of the pinned frequency scale by reading the spacing of resistance minima on the partially completed density fan as a Landau-level index ladder.
Found the result inconclusive: the admixed transverse component shifts the minima so that integer-index assignment is ambiguous.
The spacing found was only consistent with, not an independent confirmation of, the frequency-derived scale.
Found a tone at the sum frequency present and dominant in every fan column.
Combined it with the two fundamental branches across the whole swept density range to pin a single global density/lever-arm scale of 0.93 +- 0.03.
This refines an earlier single-density estimate of 0.90.
No sign of the pinned scale being off by a factor of two or four.
Inferred the measured pickup signal on this contact pair carries an admixture of a Hall-like component on top of the longitudinal resistance (estimated admixture fraction ~0.2).
Based on the raw trace going negative near 2-4 T and climbing in a staircase up to about 600 ohm by 10 T.
Used this to argue that filling-factor assignment and low-field oscillation-spacing checks on this pair cannot serve as an independent calibration cross-check.
On the completed higher-quality map, a third oscillation branch resolves directly across roughly ten densities.
This branch traces its own shallow density-dependent frequency trend, distinct from the half-frequency modulation component identified earlier.
The previously ambiguous, polynomial-degree-sensitive low-frequency reading is now attributed to a magnetoresistance background component contaminating the sub-1-tesla region.
This attribution follows once that region is explicitly excluded from the fit, rather than relying on polynomial degree alone.
The two branches (original main branch plus newly resolved light branch) together close the expected total carrier density at one shared overall scale.
This shared scale sits at the edge of, but still inside, the previously established scale range.
Final campaign call for the device's wired voltage-probe pair (probing the two series-connected doping regions together): the stacking is ABAB (Bernal), rated 'strong.'
Based on the closing Luttinger frequency sum.
Based on both SdH branches tracking the ABAB model's density dependence across the fan.
Based on the combination-tone origin of the summed frequency.
Based on the Lifshitz-Kosevich mass split (light mass matching the model exactly, with a decisive beat exclusion).
Hedge: the heavy-branch mass remains an unresolved extraction-window fork.
Hedge: only a single voltage-probe pair was available, so a different stacking confined to the weakly-doped secondary region cannot be excluded.
Measured heavy-to-light mass ratio (about 1.2-1.4) falls well short of the favored stacking model's predicted ratio (~2.2) at this density.
Flagged explicitly as not matching the model's specific mass-ratio prediction.
Treated as a hedge on the stacking call rather than evidence for a different stacking order.
Reason: the lighter branch's mass rests on a short, low-resolution frequency record, called the softest number in the analysis.
Reason: no competing model was judged able to reproduce the full observed pattern of frequencies, partition, and masses together.
Decided to proceed to the physics sweeps at zero silicon-gate voltage rather than pursue further contact-doping attempts.
Treated the fixed source contact resistance as a normalization problem rather than a blocking failure.

For the remainder of the campaign, longitudinal resistance channels are computed by dividing each channel's voltage by the measured drain current at that point, rather than by assuming the nominal bias-resistor current.
The charge-neutrality point is located near the middle of the swept gate's range on the two more sensitive longitudinal-resistance channels.
It shows a clear peak roughly 3-5x the flanking resistance on those two channels.
A third, weaker channel shows the same peak shape at about 15% of the amplitude and at a measurably offset gate voltage.
The drain current stays near its target value throughout.
Resolved a spectral branch present in every fan column, rising monotonically from ~3.2 T to 6.9 T across the swept density range.
This branch sits at a roughly constant fraction (0.21-0.22) of the sum-frequency tone.
It matches a candidate stacking model's predicted low-frequency branch.
Its density slope (~3.3 T per 10^12 cm^-2) was judged far steeper than a competing bilayer-plus-monolayer model's predicted low-frequency-branch slope (~1 T per 10^12 cm^-2).
This disfavors the competing bilayer-plus-monolayer assignment for this branch.
Interpreted the two lower oscillation frequencies as fundamentals of two distinct Fermi-surface pockets.
Their sum (6.2+21.8=28.0 T) matches the observed higher-frequency peak (28.1 T).
Their difference (21.8-6.2=15.6 T) matches the observed lowest-frequency peak (15.6 T).
This sum-and-difference intermodulation set is read as consistent with inter-pocket magnetic breakdown, rather than an artifact of two separate, non-interacting current paths.
Resolved a second, higher-frequency spectral branch only above roughly half the design density range (about 20.8-25.2 T, roughly 0.77 of the sum-frequency tone).
This matches the same stacking model's predicted high-frequency branch (~0.79).
Below that density range, this branch could not be separated from the sum-frequency tone given the achieved frequency resolution.
Stated as unresolved rather than absent below that density range.
Converted the session's pinned overall frequency/lever-arm scale into an absolute top-gate capacitance corresponding to roughly a 10.2 nm hBN-equivalent dielectric thickness.
Offered this as an updated calibration figure alongside the corresponding back-gate capacitance.
The lowest newly-added temperature rung equilibrated stably just below the fixed lower edge of the acceptance band, and the guard timed out into a safe fault (heaters switched off, no hardware risk).

Redefined the rung-acceptance rule from a fixed absolute-temperature target to a stability/monotonicity criterion (bounded drift over a hold window, minimum monotonic step from previous rung, wide sanity fence).
Purpose: so a genuinely stable but off-nominal rung is accepted and logged rather than faulted.
Resumed the ladder from the next rung without repeating the already-completed base point.
Temperature ladder shows non-activated behavior at the reference and weakly-gapped points.
Temperature ladder shows only modest, saturating activation at the two most-gapped points.

This is read as confirming the zero-field resistance plateau is a property of the small-gap channel itself (finite, thermally assisted sub-gap conduction), rather than an external parallel-conduction path.
Argued the sum-frequency tone is a magnetic-breakdown/intermodulation feature rather than a sampling artifact.
Its strength relative to the higher fundamental branch grows across field windows in the earlier single-density sweep.
Its strength relative to the higher fundamental branch also grows across field windows in a matching fan column.
The same three-tone pattern reproduces under two different field-sampling grids.
Flagged the field-window test as only weakly informative below about half the design density range, where the two peaks merge.
Charge-neutrality-point resistance grows substantially with displacement field along the fitted ridge, roughly doubling from the field-symmetric point to the most extreme field sampled on the map.
This pattern is flagged as consistent with a displacement-field-tunable gap of the kind expected for one specific stacking order.
Explicitly noted the achieved electron temperature is too high for this alone to diagnose a gap.
The observation is carried forward only as a supporting/domain caveat, referenced again after the electron-side spot check and in the final call's hedge list.
Designed a density-versus-field map riding the field down from 10 T to 2.4 T at uniform steps in inverse field (36 rows).
Stepped the gate point along the zero-displacement-field line from a design density of about 3.4 down to 1.5x10^12 cm^-2 (41 points per row).
Used a fixed (not autoranged) pickup sensitivity.
Chose to end the sweep parked at 2.4 T rather than retraverse back to 10 T.
Chose to run a cheap 1D gate-voltage cut through the charge-neutrality point (other gate parked at zero) before committing to the full 2D gate map.
Purpose: to check whether the neutrality ridge resolves at all.
Purpose: to measure the achievable point rate.
Using the density calibration from the first field-ramp sweep with no free parameters, the second sweep's roughly 204 resistance minima fell in steps of two rather than four.
This is read as the displacement field lifting a two-fold degeneracy of the Landau levels.
The zero-filling-factor state grew monotonically with field, with no crossings.
This is consistent with the field having polarized the zero-energy manifold, rather than leaving it in the crossing regime seen at zero displacement field.
The device is inert to silicon-gate doping across the full bipolar card-limit range: drain current stays pinned near its baseline with no hysteresis on the overlapping segment.
Phase readback on one channel (~172 deg +/- 4 deg) is consistent with a resistive, in-phase signal through an inverting stage.
Current scaling across three drive frequencies is consistent with a genuine resistive, non-capacitive, non-barrier-like path.
Linearity across three drive amplitudes is also consistent with a genuine resistive, non-capacitive, non-barrier-like path.
Current is confirmed to reach the downstream voltage probes, which read drive-proportional signals.
This means the fixed resistance is a real contact element, not an open/blocked device.

The physical zero of displacement field was located from the symmetry vertex of the dominant ridge's resistance minimum plotted against raw displacement field (vertex at roughly +0.012-0.013 V/nm raw).
This offset was adopted as the D=0 reference for all subsequent gate-voltage-to-(n,D) conversions.
Designed a temperature ladder from base temperature up to 50 K, at five displacement-field points spanning the reference point and both gapped and near-neutral settings identified by the fine map.

Purpose: to measure the thermal activation of the field-induced gap and settle whether it matches the meV scale expected for one candidate stacking order or the much larger scale expected for another.
Purpose: separately, to determine whether the zero-field plateau's resistance is thermally activated (a real gap) or temperature-independent (a residual/parallel conduction path).
Launched the first zero-field 2D gate map, sweeping one gate over its full card-limit range on the fast axis.
Swept the other gate over a reduced window (about half its card-limit range) on the slow axis.
This traded full coverage of the second gate (which would add roughly three more hours) for keeping the neutrality line inside the fast-axis window over the density range the campaign actually needs.
Decided the hole side of the zero-displacement-field line would not be pursued further this session.
Reported as geometry-limited on this contact pair rather than as a null measurement.
Reason: the auxiliary gate could not remove the series-segment confound.
Held the auxiliary gate at 0 V for the remainder of the session.
The first attempt at the field-ramp sweep failed on a data-writer bug after the ramp had already been started.
Chose to relaunch the same measurement riding the ramp in progress from its current field (about 0.7 T), rather than returning the magnet to zero field first.
Accepted the loss of the lowest-field portion of the sweep.
Judgment: the lost interval (0-0.7 T) was below where the Landau levels of interest would be resolvable.
Because the neutrality point was not found in the top-gate cut, chose to sweep the back gate next (at zero top-gate voltage) rather than go straight to a full 2D map.
Reasoning: a geometry-based lever-arm estimate indicated the back gate reaches further into the hole side.
This made it the cheaper way to locate the neutrality point.
Delivered the campaign's final stacking determination for the measured contact pair as one particular stacking order.
Stated strength: 'strong, not decisive.'
Read a resistance minimum at 7.3 T as a high-field quantum-Hall filling factor of about 16 on the pinned frequency scale.
Described this as consistent with a Landau-level ladder member for a four-layer stack.
Judged minima below filling factor 12 on this pair unreadable because of the admixed transverse component.
Called this evidence weak at most.
Chose to sweep the silicon gate through zero to the opposite polarity's card limit.
Reasoning: if the contact metal dopes the leads one way, the opposite gate polarity might open them where the first polarity did not.
The sweep overlaps the first leg's range as an in-situ hysteresis check.
